question: Does the Q8_0 quality-gate failure of Pythia-14M come from the embedding and output-head matrices or from the linear layers?

pre_registration.corpus: WikiText-2 raw test split, whole split, tokenised with the model's own tokenizer (hashes in the run reports)
pre_registration.tool: thme evaluate, --eval-context 1024, default quality gate (max perplexity rise 0.45), --device auto

groups.L: attention qkv, attention output, MLP up, MLP down in layers 0 to 5

variants: E at Q8_0, L as stored
L at Q8_0, E as stored
E at Q4_0, L as stored
L at Q4_0, E as stored
pre_registration.unchanged: norms and biases (1-D tensors) stay as stored in every variant
pre_registration.reproduction_check: E and L at Q8_0 must reproduce the committed uniform Q8_0 rise of +0.8335 (verification_report.json) within 0.02 perplexity; if not, the report says so and the device difference is named as the first suspect, not hidden
pre_registration.rule: At Q8_0 the group (E or L) whose single-group variant has the larger perplexity rise over the unquantised baseline is called the cause of the failure. A group 'fails alone' if its single-group rise exceeds 0.45. The same comparison at Q4_0 is reported as secondary. If the two single-group rises differ by less than 20 percent of the larger one, the result is called 'both contribute' instead of naming one cause.
pre_registration.also_reported: additivity (rise of E alone plus rise of L alone versus rise of both), bytes of the written GGUF per variant, the quality-gate verdict per variant, device, adapter and driver as the run report records them
